A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLSU benchmark and framework. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material reorganized in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of eleven VLMs, structured prompting experiments, modality comparisons, error analyses, and refusal/helpfulness measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds benchmark/model results in Table 11 and annotation-agreement measurements in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The three severity levels, 17 safety patterns, four-stage dataset pipeline, and structured CoT procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C newly documents generation signatures, concept augmentation, and sampling details without establishing a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Table 11 adds actual evaluations on ELITE, VLGuard, and MLLMGuard, substantially broadening external benchmark coverage across datasets with different image sources and safety-pattern distributions. VLSU itself retains 8,187 samples, 15 harm categories, and 17 patterns; expanded illustrations do not establish additional VLSU data.

E2.justification: v2 adds the GLM4.1V-9B reasoning model to the benchmark comparison, including results on VLSU and the three previously evaluated external benchmarks. The original eleven evaluated models remain represented.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix A.6 states that every text/joint sample receives three annotations; v2 B.4 reports three graders for 92.4% of samples and two for the remainder. This revises the reported reference-label construction setting, without establishing that evaluations were rerun. Existing classification prompts, CoT procedures, and inference settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an analysis of annotation reliability across the 17 safety patterns, while Appendix A.3 adds harm-category/severity composition breakdowns. Existing prompting, unimodal-versus-joint, error-type, and refusal/helpfulness analyses are retained, largely relocated to Appendix E.

E5.justification: The existing 10,000-iteration bootstrap procedure remains. v2 additionally reports Krippendorff's alpha, overall pairwise agreement, and pattern-specific agreement with 95% confidence intervals in Table 9. No increased model-run count or new seed-based evaluation is reported.

E6.justification: Table 11 substantially expands reported F1 results, including GLM4.1V's 51.9 on VLSU and 99.8 on MSTS, and results on three added benchmarks. Annotation statistics are also newly reported. Original main-table results remain unchanged, but some duplicated entries conflict: Gemini-1.5's MM-SafetyBench F1 is 78.3 in Table 11 versus 82.4 in Table 1. These discrepancies do not establish performance changes.

T1.justification: The safety-tuple formulation and 27-to-17 combination framework are unchanged. v2 B.4 adds a mathematical chance-agreement assertion under a uniform four-label prior, giving 1/16. This is a localized addition to the reasoning and is incorrect for independent uniform labels, whose probability of agreeing on any label is 1/4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: a borderline-aware benchmark, systematic joint-understanding failures, refusal tradeoffs, and limited benefits from structured prompting. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies English-only text as a limitation and notes that other languages may introduce different safety considerations. The datasheet also discusses potential guardrail and alignment-training uses. Interpretations of the existing model experiments remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C, and F substantially expand construction and reproducibility documentation: generation signatures, query-type weights, a 3.6-billion-image source corpus, annotator qualifications and safeguards, label filtering, dataset fields, and distribution terms. v1's 'link coming soon' is replaced by a stated dataset access location. Existing evaluation prompts and hardware settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MLLMGuard, VLGuard, ELITE, and Datasheets for Datasets. Table 8 extends comparison of prior datasets' provenance, labeling, and safety coverage. The main related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized from one sequence of subsections into six thematic appendices with a contents list. Existing results and evaluation instructions move into dedicated sections, alongside extensive explanatory documentation. Main-text editing is limited mainly to cross-references, terminology, and the new limitation paragraph.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 10 is expanded into separate severity-specific example figures. v2 adds annotation-guideline illustrations, a harm-category chart, and tables for category distributions, dataset comparisons, agreement, and extended results. Existing diagnostic plots are retained as Figures 16–18, while the main figures and tables remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes dataset construction and annotation substantially more auditable than v1's brief descriptions, and broadens empirical comparison. However, conflicting retained scores in Tables 1 and 11 and the incorrect chance-agreement assertion in B.4 weaken confidence in the added validation. The documentation gains support a net improvement, but these reporting problems temper its overall significance.
